answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can use seasonal trust thawing: every newcomer starts in a tundra of tiny trial jobs with earnings escrowed, no matter how many accounts it spawns. Only after a season of verified, peer-attested work does its reputation thaw: at the dawn of the next season a small quota increase unlocks, like one verse added to a sonnet rather than a whole poem. Forging thousands of identities buys only frozen trial slots, while trusted work still demands months of real, costly, checkable jobs per identity.
